# 📉 CMSY++ catch-only stock assessment

CMSY++ (Froese et al. 2023), the successor of CMSY (Froese et al. 2017),
estimates MSY, Bmsy and Fmsy, and the relative stock size (B/Bmsy) and
exploitation (F/Fmsy) of every year, from a catch series, a prior for
the intrinsic growth rate r and priors for the relative biomass B/k. The
package bundles the official CMSY++ code (`CMSY++16.R`, January 2021),
its neural network and its user guide (Froese et al. 2021), and a few
functions take care of everything from installing JAGS (Plummer 2003) to
drawing the charts. The CMSY++ runs shown in this article were made
beforehand; building the article does not run CMSY++.

**FishStat has catches only, no CPUE.** The FAO capture statistics have
no abundance index (CPUE or survey biomass), so every stock is assessed
with the catch-only part of CMSY++ (CMSY, `btype = "None"`) and the
Bayesian Schaefer model (BSM) does not run. The results then depend
mostly on the B/k priors, and independent tests found that catch-only
methods classify stock status poorly with default priors (Free et
al. 2020; Ovando et al. 2021; Kell et al. 2022). The results are
**indicative** and do not replace stock assessments. As in FAO (2026),
the status has two classes only: **maximally sustainably fished**
(B/Bmsy at least 0.8 in the last year) or **overfished** (below 0.8);
catch-only results do not make a stock “underfished”.

**Disclaimer and source of CMSY++.** CMSY++ was developed by Rainer
Froese and colleagues (Froese et al. 2021, 2023). faofishingreport is
not affiliated with or endorsed by the authors of CMSY++. The package
bundles the authors’ unmodified March 2021 release (GEOMAR OceanRep,
record [52147](https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/), CC BY 4.0),
whose code is also published on GitHub at
<https://github.com/SISTA16/cmsyPlusPlus>.
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)
runs a copy of it with only the changes listed in `code_changes.csv` of
each run folder (operating-system settings, no automatic package
installation), which leave the method unchanged. Questions on the method
go to the authors of CMSY++; problems with how this package runs it go
to the [faofishingreport
issues](https://github.com/Linbojun99/faofishingreport/issues). Users
are responsible for checking and interpreting the results.

## ⚙️ Common arguments

These arguments have the same meaning in all CMSY functions that have
them; the tables of each function below list its other arguments.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `stocks` | Stocks to use: `Stock` identifiers (e.g. `"PRA_27"`) or species, by English or Chinese FAO name, scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code (all stocks of the species) | `NULL`: all stocks |
| `table` | Save the tables (in `tables/cmsy/`) | `TRUE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text, names and table columns: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) (`"en"` unless changed) |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files (in `figures/pptx/cmsy/`) | `FALSE`; `fao_settings(pptx = TRUE)` changes it for all functions |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |
| `annotations` | Text added to the axis titles and labels: `FALSE` none, `TRUE` all, or any of `"title"`, `"subtitle"`, `"caption"`, `"legend"` and `"labels"` (text inside the chart) | `FALSE`; `options(faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations = TRUE)` changes it for the session |
| `silent` | Print no progress bars and messages | `FALSE`; `fao_settings(silent = TRUE)` changes it for the session |
| `data_dir` | Folder where downloads are kept | [`fao_data_dir()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_data_dir.md) |

## 🚀 One step: cmsy_area()

``` r

cmsy_setup()                                                     # once: JAGS and the R packages
area27 <- cmsy_area("Atlantic, Northeast", top = 10)
```

[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
does Steps 4 to 7 and Step 9 below in one call: it takes the `top`
species with the largest catch of the last `recent_years` years of a
fishing area (or the species given in `species`), prepares the input,
runs CMSY++, draws all charts, projects the stocks and writes the
tables, with a progress bar for each step. Main species that cannot be
assessed (e.g. without an r prior) are listed with the reason. `area`
can name several areas; each gets its own folder in `out_dir`, sorted
into:

    cmsy_areas/Atlantic__Eastern_Central/
    ├── input/      CMSY++ catch and ID files (catch.csv, id.csv), the stocks assessed (stocks.csv)
    │               and the main species left out with the reason (excluded.csv)
    ├── runs/       CMSY++ output of each stock (JPEG charts, cmsy_output.csv, log.txt), the changed
    │               code and the list of changes (code_changes.csv)
    ├── figures/    a folder of charts per stock and summary/ (figures_pptx/ with pptx = TRUE)
    └── tables/     results.csv, series.csv, priors_table.csv, results_table.csv, forecast.csv,
                    forecast_share.csv, settings_used.csv and sources.csv

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `area` | FAO major fishing area name(s), as in [`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md) (e.g. `"Atlantic, Eastern Central"`), or FAO catch data such as `fishing_area_data()$area_data` | required |
| `top` | Number of species with the largest catch to assess | `10` |
| `species` | Species to assess instead of the `top` ones: English or Chinese name, scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code | `NULL` |
| `recent_years` | Species are ranked by their mean catch over the last `recent_years` years of the data | `10` |
| `out_dir` | Folder in which a folder per area is made | `"cmsy_areas"` |
| `auto_start` | Start a stock in the year suggested by CMSY++ when its start biomass is ambiguous (see Step 5) | `TRUE` (`FALSE` in [`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)) |
| `seed` | Random seed, so runs can be repeated with the same results | `1` |
| `parallel` | Number of stocks run at the same time; each uses two more processes for its two MCMC chains | `NULL`: half the processor cores |
| `settings` | CMSY++ settings that replace its defaults (see [The settings of CMSY++](#cmsy-settings)) | [`list()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html): none |
| `charts` | Charts to draw (see Step 6) | all charts |
| `classes` | Status classes: `"fao"` (two) or `"palomares"` (five) | `"fao"` |
| `forecast` | Also project the stocks under the default scenarios of [`cmsy_forecast()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_forecast.md) | `TRUE` |
| `annotations`, `lang`, `pptx`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |
| `...` | Further arguments of [`cmsy_input()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_input.md), e.g. `priors`, `default_resilience` or `min_years` |  |

[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
runs CMSY++ without the retrospective analysis, so its retrospective
chart is skipped (see Step 5). It returns the result of
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)
with `input`, `forecast`, `tables` and `dir` (the folder of the area);
for several areas, a list of these named by area. On a Mac with Apple
silicon, the ten main species of area 27 take about a minute from input
to tables.

## 💻 Step 1: check the computer and adapt the settings

The CMSY++ code was written on Windows. Its user guide (step 12) tells
Mac users to change every `windows()` to
[`quartz()`](https://rdrr.io/r/grDevices/quartz.html) and
`antialias = "cleartype"` to `"default"`. The code tests for Windows
with `grepl("win", sysname)`, which is also true for macOS (“Darwin”),
so on a Mac it calls `windows()` and stops.
[`cmsy_system()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_system.md)
finds the operating system, R version, processor, JAGS and R packages,
and shows the settings
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)
will use:

``` r

sys <- cmsy_system()
show_table(sys$changes)
```

| change | applies_to | what |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Package installation | all | Lines that install missing packages on every run are removed (cmsy_setup() installs them). |
| snpar | all | library(snpar) is removed and snpar::runs.test() is replaced by the same approximate runs test, reproduced from snpar 1.0 (Debin Qiu, GPL \>= 2; archived on CRAN on 2022-05-10: <https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/snpar/>; source mirror: <https://github.com/cran/snpar>). |
| Working directory | all | setwd(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()\$path) is removed, so RStudio is not needed; each stock runs in its own folder. |
| Settings | all | File names, the stock, the chart switches and the general settings (CMSY++ defaults unless changed with cmsy_run(settings = ), including the MCMC iterations of the JAGS call) are set by cmsy_run() after the original settings section. |
| Chart windows | linux | The test grepl(“win”, sysname), which is also true on macOS (“Darwin”), is replaced; windows(): changed to an off-screen device, so charts are drawn and saved without opening windows. |
| JPEG antialias | linux | antialias = “cleartype” (Windows only) is changed to “default” (user guide, step 12). |
| Results for charts | all | After the main analysis of a stock, its priors, the posterior draws of r, k and B/k, the yearly estimates with 95% limits and the last-year Kobe draws are saved to cmsy_extra.rds (retrospective runs to cmsy_retro.rds) for cmsy_plot(); no calculation is changed. |

The changes are made to a copy of the code written into each run folder
(`CMSY++16_faofishingreport.R`, with the list in `code_changes.csv`);
the bundled original never changes. Charts are drawn on an off-screen
device by default, which saves the JPEG files on every system without
opening windows; `device = "screen"` uses the system’s own window
instead (`windows()`,
[`quartz()`](https://rdrr.io/r/grDevices/quartz.html) or
[`x11()`](https://rdrr.io/r/grDevices/x11.html)). If the detection is
wrong, set the system:

``` r

cmsy_system(os = "windows")                       # settings used on Windows
options(faofishingreport.cmsy_os = "macos")       # for the whole session
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `os` | Operating system whose settings are used: `"auto"` (detect it), `"windows"`, `"macos"` or `"linux"` | `"auto"` |
| `device` | Where CMSY++ draws its charts before saving them as JPEG files: `"file"` (an off-screen device that works on every system and in batch runs) or `"screen"` (the system’s own window) | `"file"` |
| `jags` | JAGS version to recommend: `"recommended"` (the newest JAGS 4 for this R version, which works with rjags from CRAN), `"latest"` (JAGS 5.0.0, which needs rjags 5 from SourceForge) or a version number such as `"4.3.2"` | `"recommended"` |
| `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

It returns the system (`os`, `os_detected`, `arch`, `r_version`), the
installed `jags` and `rjags` versions, the `packages` table, the
recommended `jags_installer` and `rjags_source`, the chart `device` and
`antialias`, and the `changes` made to the CMSY++ code.

## 🧰 Step 2: install JAGS and the R packages

``` r

cmsy_setup()
```

[`cmsy_setup()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_setup.md)
asks before installing anything, then:

1.  installs the missing R packages from CRAN (R2jags, rjags, coda,
    gplots, mvtnorm, neuralnet, conicfit); snpar, archived on CRAN on
    2022-05-10, is replaced by the same approximate runs test,
    reproduced from snpar 1.0 (Debin Qiu, GPL ≥ 2; [CRAN
    archive](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/snpar/),
    source mirror <https://github.com/cran/snpar>);
2.  downloads the JAGS installer for the system and R version from its
    pinned link, checks its size and MD5 checksum and opens it (`.exe`
    on Windows, `.pkg` on macOS; on Linux it downloads the source and
    shows the commands). JAGS is a separate program: restart R after
    installing it and run
    [`cmsy_setup()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_setup.md)
    again to check;
3.  checks the bundled CMSY++ files.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `jags` | JAGS version: `"recommended"`, `"latest"` or a version number (as in [`cmsy_system()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_system.md)) | `"recommended"` |
| `os` | Operating system: `"auto"`, `"windows"`, `"macos"` or `"linux"` | `"auto"` |
| `ask` | Ask before installing anything; in a non-interactive session nothing is installed when `ask` is `TRUE` | `TRUE` |
| `data_dir`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

It returns the result of
[`cmsy_system()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_system.md)
after the installation. JAGS 4.3.2 (4.3.1 for older R versions) is the
default because rjags on CRAN (4-17) needs JAGS 4. The newest JAGS,
5.0.0, needs rjags 5-3 from SourceForge: `cmsy_setup(jags = "latest")`.
Installers copied into `inst/jags/` of the package source are used
instead of downloading. Versions, links, sizes, checksums, licences and
references of every component are listed by
[`cmsy_sources()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_sources.md):

``` r

src <- cmsy_sources()
show_table(src[, c("component", "version", "platform", "file", "license", "url")], n = 30)
```

### The R version and the JAGS version must match

JAGS is a separate program that rjags uses for the MCMC. On Windows and
macOS each JAGS installer is built for a range of R versions; with the
wrong one rjags cannot be loaded and CMSY++ cannot run. rjags on CRAN
(4-17) needs JAGS 4. The matches (JAGS 4 is the default):

| System | R version | JAGS installer | rjags |
|----|----|----|----|
| Windows | 4.5, 4.6 | `JAGS-4.3.2.exe` | 4-17 (CRAN) |
| Windows | 4.2 to 4.4 | `JAGS-4.3.1.exe` | 4-17 (CRAN) |
| macOS | 4.3 and later | `JAGS-4.3.2.pkg` | 4-17 (CRAN) |
| macOS | 4.2 | `JAGS-4.3.1.pkg` | 4-15 or later (the CRAN binary for R 4.2 stays at 4-15) |
| Linux | any | the system package (e.g. `sudo apt-get install jags`) or `JAGS-4.3.2.tar.gz` | 4-17 (CRAN, built from source) |
| Windows | 4.5, 4.6 | `JAGS-5.0.0.exe` (optional, newest) | 5-3 (SourceForge, not yet on CRAN) |
| macOS | 4.3 and later | `JAGS-5.0.0-universal.pkg` (optional) | 5-3 (SourceForge: binary for R 4.6, else from source) |

The rules come from the README of the JAGS downloads (e.g. the Windows
build of JAGS 4.3.2 “was built with Rtools45 and is suitable for
interfacing with R 4.5.x”; “JAGS-4.3.2.pkg for compatibility with R
version 4.3.0 and later”; “JAGS-4.3.1.pkg for compatibility with R
versions 4.0.x to 4.2.x”), and each combination is installed and run
with CMSY++ by the package’s GitHub Actions workflow.
[`cmsy_jags_versions()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_jags_versions.md)
gives the table, marks the row for this computer and gives the evidence
and README link of each rule:

``` r

jv <- cmsy_jags_versions()
show_table(jv[, c("system", "r_versions", "jags", "installer", "rjags", "default", "this_computer")], n = 10)
```

| system | r_versions | jags | installer | rjags | default | this_computer |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Windows | 4.5 to 4.6.x | 4.3.2 | JAGS-4.3.2.exe | 4-17 (CRAN) | TRUE | FALSE |
| Windows | 4.2 to 4.4.x | 4.3.1 | JAGS-4.3.1.exe | 4-17 (CRAN) | TRUE | FALSE |
| macOS | \>= 4.3 | 4.3.2 | JAGS-4.3.2.pkg | 4-17 (CRAN) | TRUE | FALSE |
| macOS | 4.0 to 4.2.x | 4.3.1 | JAGS-4.3.1.pkg | 4-15 or later (CRAN; its binary for R 4.2 is 4-15) | TRUE | FALSE |
| Linux | \>= 4.2 | 4.3.2 | JAGS-4.3.2.tar.gz | 4-17 (CRAN, built from source) | TRUE | TRUE |
| Windows | 4.5 to 4.6.x | 5.0.0 | JAGS-5.0.0.exe | 5-3 (SourceForge, Windows binary) | FALSE | FALSE |
| macOS | \>= 4.3 | 5.0.0 | JAGS-5.0.0-universal.pkg | 5-3 (SourceForge: binary for R 4.6, else source) | FALSE | FALSE |
| Linux | \>= 4.2 | 5.0.0 | JAGS-5.0.0.tar.gz | 5-3 (SourceForge, source) | FALSE | FALSE |

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `os` | `"all"`, or one system: `"auto"` (this computer), `"windows"`, `"macos"` or `"linux"` | `"all"` |
| `r_version` | R version marked as `this_computer` | [`getRversion()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/numeric_version.html): the running R |
| `silent` | Do not print the match for this computer | see [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |

No need to look it up:
[`cmsy_download_jags()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_download_jags.md)
picks the installer for the system, R version and processor, downloads
it and checks its size, MD5 and SHA-256; for JAGS 5 it also downloads
rjags 5-3. The files are kept in `fao_data_dir()/cmsy/downloads`, so
they are downloaded only once. It can also download for other systems or
R versions, e.g. to prepare installers for computers without internet.
[`cmsy_install_jags()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_install_jags.md)
downloads the installer and opens it:

``` r

cmsy_download_jags()                                        # the JAGS for this computer
cmsy_download_jags(version = "latest")                      # JAGS 5.0.0 and rjags 5-3
cmsy_download_jags(os = "all", r_version = "4.4.1", dest = "jags_installers")   # all systems, R 4.4
cmsy_install_jags()                                         # download and open the installer
```

[`cmsy_download_jags()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_download_jags.md):

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `version` | `"recommended"` (JAGS 4 for this R version), `"latest"` (JAGS 5.0.0 with rjags 5-3) or a JAGS version such as `"4.3.1"` | `"recommended"` |
| `os` | `"auto"` (this computer), `"windows"`, `"macos"`, `"linux"` or `"all"` (the installers of the three systems for `r_version`) | `"auto"` |
| `r_version` | R version the installer is for | [`getRversion()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/numeric_version.html): the running R |
| `arch` | Processor, for the rjags 5 binary on macOS: `"auto"`, `"arm64"` (Apple silicon) or `"x86_64"` (Intel) | `"auto"` |
| `dest` | Folder to copy the files to | `NULL`: none |
| `rjags` | Also download the rjags package needed by JAGS 5 (rjags 4-17 for JAGS 4 comes from CRAN through [`cmsy_setup()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_setup.md)) | `TRUE` |
| `data_dir`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

It returns a table with one row per file: system, R version, component,
version, file, local path, link, SHA-256 and whether the checksums
matched.

[`cmsy_install_jags()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_install_jags.md):

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `version` | `"recommended"`, `"latest"` or a version number | `"recommended"` |
| `os` | `"auto"`, `"windows"`, `"macos"` or `"linux"` | `"auto"` |
| `open` | Open the installer (`.exe` on Windows, `.pkg` on macOS; on Linux the commands to install JAGS are shown) | `TRUE` |
| `data_dir`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

It returns the path of the downloaded installer; an installer placed in
`inst/jags/` of the package source is used instead of downloading.

## 🐟 Step 3: priors for r from FishBase and SeaLifeBase

A built-in table gives the resilience and prior r of the 3,155
species-level items of the FAO capture statistics in FishBase or
SeaLifeBase (release 26.06). It can be searched offline by English,
Chinese or scientific name or by 3-alpha code, and every row links to
its source page (`open = TRUE` opens the pages). How FishBase and
SeaLifeBase data are obtained and matched to FAO names is explained in
[🐠 FishBase and SeaLifeBase
traits](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/fishbase.md).

``` r

cod <- cmsy_priors("Gadus morhua")
show_table(cod[, c("species_name", "scientific_name", "SpecCode", "resilience", "prior_r",
                   "r_low", "r_high", "r_source", "url")])
```

| species_name | scientific_name | SpecCode | resilience | prior_r | r_low | r_high | r_source | url |
|:---|:---|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|:---|:---|
| Atlantic cod | Gadus morhua | 69 | Medium | 0.51 | 0.34 | 0.76 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 66 full stock assessments.) | <https://www.fishbase.se/summary/69> |

The r range follows the CMSY++ user guide:

| Case | r range | Source |
|----|----|----|
| The species has a prior r in FishBase or SeaLifeBase (“Estimates based on models”) | The 95% confidence limits of the prior r | User guide Table 1 (“alternatively and better”) |
| Only the resilience is known | High 0.6–1.5; Medium 0.2–0.8; Low 0.05–0.5; Very low 0.015–0.1 | User guide Table 2 |
| Neither | No default: the user gives it (e.g. r close to 2M or 2Fmsy) | User guide Table 1 |

FAO names are matched as valid species names, then through each
database’s own synonym table; ambiguous synonyms and genus or family
items get no values. When FishBase lists several stocks of a species
with different resilience, the species-wide value is used and the others
are given in `resilience_note`.

``` r

priors <- cmsy_priors()
table(priors$match_type)
#> 
#> ambiguous synonym             exact     not a species         not found 
#>                 3              3071                 2                43 
#>           synonym 
#>                36
table(!is.na(priors$r_source))
#> 
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>   462  2693
```

Species can be named by English or Chinese FAO name, both together (as
shown with `lang = "both"`), scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code, in
[`cmsy_priors()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_priors.md),
`cmsy_input(species = )`, `cmsy_run(stocks = )` and
`cmsy_plot(stocks = )`: full names are matched first (ignoring case),
then parts of names; if several species match, they are listed so a more
precise name or code can be given. `lang` sets the language of the
results; `species_en` and `species_zh` always give both names.

``` r

p <- cmsy_priors(c("COD", "Clupea harengus", "Atlantic mackerel", "小鳍鳕"), lang = "both")
show_table(p[, c("species_name", "scientific_name", "alpha3", "r_low", "r_high", "url", "data_url", "rule_url")])
```

| species_name | scientific_name | alpha3 | r_low | r_high | url | data_url | rule_url |
|:---|:---|:---|---:|---:|:---|:---|:---|
| 大西洋鳕 Atlantic cod | Gadus morhua | COD | 0.34 | 0.76 | <https://www.fishbase.se/summary/69> | <https://data.source.coop/cboettig/fishbase/fb/v26.06/parquet/estimate.parquet> | <https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/> |
| 大西洋鲱 Atlantic herring | Clupea harengus | HER | 0.29 | 0.65 | <https://www.fishbase.se/summary/24> | <https://data.source.coop/cboettig/fishbase/fb/v26.06/parquet/estimate.parquet> | <https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/> |
| 大西洋鲭 Atlantic mackerel | Scomber scombrus | MAC | 0.28 | 0.64 | <https://www.fishbase.se/summary/118> | <https://data.source.coop/cboettig/fishbase/fb/v26.06/parquet/estimate.parquet> | <https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/> |
| 小鳍鳕 Blue whiting(=Poutassou) | Micromesistius poutassou | WHB | 0.31 | 0.70 | <https://www.fishbase.se/summary/31> | <https://data.source.coop/cboettig/fishbase/fb/v26.06/parquet/estimate.parquet> | <https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/> |

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `species` | Names to search for: English, Chinese or scientific names, FAO 3-alpha codes, or parts of them (e.g. `"Atlantic cod"`, `"Gadus morhua"`, `"COD"`, `"cod"`) | `NULL`: all rows |
| `open` | Open the FishBase or SeaLifeBase pages of the rows found (at most 10) in the browser | `FALSE` |
| `lang` | Language of the `species_name` column: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |

Every row links to its sources: `url`, the FishBase or SeaLifeBase page
of the species (where resilience and prior r can be checked);
`data_url`, the FishBase or SeaLifeBase table the value was read from
(`estimate` for prior r, `stocks` for resilience); and `rule_url`, the
CMSY++ user guide, whose Tables 1 and 2 turn the values into the r
range. The results of
[`cmsy_input()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_input.md)
and
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)
add `fao_data_url`, the FAO data release used.

## 🧾 Step 4: FAO data to CMSY++ input files

``` r

input <- cmsy_input(FAO27$area_data)
input
#> CMSY++ input from FAO capture 2026.1.0: 220 stocks ready, 534 left out
#>   Stock                  species_en                area first_year last_year
#>  HER_27            Atlantic herring Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  COD_27                Atlantic cod Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  CAP_27                     Capelin Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  WHB_27    Blue whiting(=Poutassou) Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  MAC_27           Atlantic mackerel Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  SPR_27              European sprat Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  POK_27            Saithe(=Pollock) Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  HAD_27                     Haddock Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  NOP_27                 Norway pout Atlantic, Northeast       1959      2024
#>  PIL_27 European pilchard(=Sardine) Atlantic, Northeast       1950      2024
#>  Resilience r.low  r.hi
#>      Medium 0.288 0.654
#>      Medium 0.336 0.764
#>      Medium 0.412 0.937
#>      Medium 0.307 0.698
#>      Medium 0.283 0.644
#>      Medium 0.318 0.722
#>      Medium 0.344 0.781
#>      Medium 0.328 0.746
#>      Medium 0.329 0.747
#>      Medium 0.415 0.942
```

[`cmsy_input()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_input.md)
makes the two input tables of CMSY++: the catch file (`Stock`, `yr`,
`ct`, `bt`) and the ID file (one row per stock, with its priors and
settings). It also returns the table of stocks (`stocks`) and of stocks
left out with the reason (`excluded`), and with `table = TRUE` saves the
four tables in `tables/cmsy/` (`<area>_cmsy_catch.csv`, `..._id.csv`,
`..._stocks.csv` and `..._excluded.csv`). Following the user guide:

- **Stock**: the catch of one species item in one fishing area summed
  over countries (`by = "area"`); `by = "country"` keeps countries
  apart. Only items identified to species and measured in tonnes are
  used.
- **Years**: years are consecutive. A stock runs from its first to its
  last year with catch, and missing or zero years in between are
  interpolated (and counted in `filled_years`).
- **Left out**: stocks with fewer than `min_years` years (CMSY++ uses
  the first and last ten years for its default priors), less than
  `min_catch` tonnes, more than `max_filled` years filled, or no r
  prior.

``` r

show_table(input$stocks[, c("Stock", "species_name", "first_year", "last_year", "filled_years",
                            "Resilience", "r.low", "r.hi", "r_source")])
```

| Stock | species_name | first_year | last_year | filled_years | Resilience | r.low | r.hi | r_source |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|---:|---:|:---|
| HER_27 | Atlantic herring | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.29 | 0.65 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 53 full stock assessments.) |
| COD_27 | Atlantic cod | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.34 | 0.76 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 66 full stock assessments.) |
| CAP_27 | Capelin | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.41 | 0.94 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 5 full stock assessments.) |
| WHB_27 | Blue whiting(=Poutassou) | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.31 | 0.70 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 9 full stock assessments.) |
| MAC_27 | Atlantic mackerel | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.28 | 0.64 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 10 full stock assessments.) |
| SPR_27 | European sprat | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.32 | 0.72 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 17 full stock assessments.) |
| POK_27 | Saithe(=Pollock) | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.34 | 0.78 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 21 full stock assessments.) |
| HAD_27 | Haddock | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.33 | 0.75 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 41 full stock assessments.) |
| NOP_27 | Norway pout | 1959 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.33 | 0.75 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 3 full stock assessments.) |
| PIL_27 | European pilchard(=Sardine) | 1950 | 2024 | 0 | Medium | 0.42 | 0.94 | FishBase prior r, 95% CL (Based on 26 full stock assessments.) |

``` r

table(input$excluded$reason)
#> 
#>                                                       fewer than 10 years 
#>                                                                        10 
#>                                             more than 20% of years filled 
#>                                                                        20 
#> no resilience or r prior: give it in `priors` or set `default_resilience` 
#>                                                                        22 
#>                                                  total catch below 1000 t 
#>                                                                       482
```

Expert priors replace the defaults, e.g. a B/k prior for the last year
as in Table 3 of the user guide, or a resilience for species without a
FishBase value:

``` r

input <- cmsy_input(FAO27$area_data, priors = data.frame(
  alpha3   = c("HER", "MAC"),
  endb.low = c(0.2, 0.01),
  endb.hi  = c(0.6, 0.4)
))
input <- cmsy_input(FAO27$area_data, default_resilience = "Medium")  # stocks without a FishBase value
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `area_data` | FAO catch data: `fishing_area_data()$area_data`, or any subset of [`load_fao_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/load_fao_data.md) | required |
| `species` | Species to keep: English or Chinese FAO name, both together, scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code | `NULL`: all species |
| `by` | `"area"`: one stock per species item and fishing area, summed over countries; `"country"`: one stock per species item, area and country | `"area"` |
| `priors` | Data frame of priors and settings that replace the defaults, one row per stock or species, identified by a `Stock`, `alpha3`, `species_en` or `species` column, with any of the ID file columns `Resilience`, `r.low`, `r.hi`, `stb.low`, `stb.hi`, `int.yr`, `intb.low`, `intb.hi`, `endb.low`, `endb.hi`, `StartYear`, `EndYear` and `Comment` (recorded as “user”) | `NULL` |
| `default_resilience` | Resilience (`"High"`, `"Medium"`, `"Low"` or `"Very low"`) for stocks whose species has no resilience or prior r | `NULL`: such stocks are left out, since the user guide gives no default |
| `min_years` | Minimum number of years from the first to the last year with catch | `10` |
| `min_catch` | Minimum total catch of a stock (tonnes) | `1000` |
| `max_filled` | Maximum share of the years of a stock filled by interpolation | `0.2` |
| `label` | Name at the start of the table file names | `NULL`: the fishing area (or country) of the data |
| `table`, `lang`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

## ▶️ Step 5: run CMSY++

``` r

result <- cmsy_run(input, stocks = "Pandalus borealis", auto_start = TRUE, seed = 1,
                   plots = c("analysis", "management", "kobe", "prior_posterior", "retrospective"))
result$summary
```

Each stock runs in its own folder, `cmsy/<area>_cmsy/<stock>/`
(e.g. `cmsy/Atlantic__Northeast_cmsy/PRA_27/`), and R process; the
folders keep CMSY++’s own output (`_AN.jpg`, `_MAN.jpg`, `_KOBE.jpg`,
`cmsy_output.csv`, `log.txt`), and the folder of the run has the changed
code, `code_changes.csv`, `settings_used.csv` and `sources.csv`.
`parallel` sets how many stocks run at the same time, and a progress bar
shows the stocks finished, the elapsed and the remaining time (see
“Progress bars and silent” below).

Many FAO series start in 1950 with low catches, which CMSY++ flags as
ambiguous (depleted or unexploited) and for which it suggests a start
year: the first year with 40% of the maximum catch. `auto_start = TRUE`
uses that year (CMSY++’s own `auto.start` stops with an error in
`CMSY++16.R`, so the same rule is applied to the start year before the
run, and not used if fewer than ten years would remain). The user guide
prefers setting `StartYear` or the start B/k prior (`stb.low`, `stb.hi`)
yourself in `cmsy_input(priors = )`.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `input` | The result of [`cmsy_input()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_input.md) | required |
| `stocks` | Stocks to run (see [Common arguments](#common-arguments)) | `NULL`: all stocks of `input` |
| `out_dir` | Folder for the CMSY++ output | `"cmsy"` in the working directory |
| `parallel` | Number of stocks run at the same time; each uses two more processes for its two MCMC chains | `NULL`: half the processor cores |
| `plots` | CMSY++ charts saved as JPEG files: any of `"analysis"`, `"management"`, `"kobe"`, `"prior_posterior"` and `"retrospective"` (the last two are needed by the charts of the same name in Step 6) | `c("analysis", "management", "kobe")` |
| `os`, `device` | Operating system and chart device (as in [`cmsy_system()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_system.md)) | `"auto"`, `"file"` |
| `seed` | Random seed, so runs can be repeated with the same results | `NULL` |
| `auto_start` | Start each stock in the year suggested by CMSY++ when its start biomass is ambiguous | `FALSE`, as in CMSY++ |
| `settings` | CMSY++ settings that replace its defaults (see [The settings of CMSY++](#cmsy-settings)) | [`list()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html): none |
| `timeout` | Maximum time for one stock (seconds); a stock still running after it is reported as failed | `3600` |
| `table`, `lang`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments); the tables are `tables/cmsy/<area>_cmsy_results.csv`, `..._series.csv` and `..._sources.csv` |  |

The example is the 30 stocks with the largest catch in 2015–2024 in FAO
area 27 (Northeast Atlantic), run with the start years suggested by
CMSY++ (`p_green`: probability of the green Kobe quadrant, B ≥ Bmsy and
F ≤ Fmsy, in the last year):

``` r

top30 <- read.csv(file.path(fig_dir, "..", "top30_area27.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
top30$species <- fao_translate(top30$species_en, "species", getOption("faofishingreport.lang", "en"))
show_table(top30[, c("rank", "Stock", "species", "scientific_name", "first_year", "B_Bmsy", "F_Fmsy", "p_green", "status")],
           n = 30, digits = 2)
```

Two stocks are shown in detail below: the healthiest and the most
clearly overfished.

- **Healthy: northern prawn** (*Pandalus borealis*, `PRA_27`, 14th by
  catch): last-year B/Bmsy 1.39 (95% CI 1.08–1.63), F/Fmsy 0.58, a 99%
  probability of the green quadrant.
- **Overfished: capelin** (*Mallotus villosus*, `CAP_27`, 7th by catch):
  last-year B/Bmsy 0.26 (95% CI 0.10–0.54), F/Fmsy 1.05, a 100%
  probability that B/Bmsy is below 0.8 and 52% of the red quadrant.

Capelin is a short-lived fish whose stocks rise and fall with
recruitment, and fisheries on it have been closed in some years; a
catch-only model reads such falls in catch as falls in biomass. These
are completed CMSY++ runs with the B/k priors of the neural network, not
validated stock assessments; compare them with the assessments of ICES
before using them.

Their priors and results tables, from
[`cmsy_tables()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_tables.md)
(Step 9), northern prawn first:

`result$summary` has one row per stock: MSY, Bmsy, Fmsy, r and k with
their 95% limits, the last-year B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy and biomass with their
limits, the probability of each Kobe quadrant and of B/Bmsy below 0.8
(`p_overfished`), the status in two schemes (`status`, FAO;
`status_palomares`, Palomares et al. 2018), all priors with their
sources and CMSY++’s own notes (such as `suggested_start_year`).
`result$series` gives catch, predicted catch, B/k, biomass, B/Bmsy, F
and F/Fmsy by year with 95% limits; `result$kobe` the last-year draws;
`result$details` the posterior draws of r, k and B/k, the prior
parameters and the retrospective runs; `result$settings` the CMSY++
settings used; `result$changes` the changes to the code; and
`result$sources` the versions and links of CMSY++, JAGS, R, the R
packages, the FAO data and FishBase used.

## 📊 Step 6: charts

``` r

cmsy_plot(result)
```

Based on a survey of the charts of 54 CMSY application papers,
[`cmsy_plot()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_plot.md)
draws, for each stock, every chart of the CMSY++ user guide, and the
usual summaries of several stocks, in `figures/png/cmsy/<stock>/` and
`figures/png/cmsy/summary/` (and as PowerPoint with `pptx = TRUE`). It
returns the ggplot objects.

**By default only axis titles and labels are shown**, so charts can take
report captions of their own. Titles, subtitles, captions (method, data
and prior sources), legends and text in the charts (quadrant
probabilities, PPVR, Mohn’s rho) are switched on with `annotations`:
`TRUE` for all, or e.g. `c("title", "legend")`;
`options(faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations = TRUE)` changes the session
default.

| Chart | Content |
|----|----|
| `analysis` | The six panels of the CMSY++ analysis chart (user guide Figure 1): catch and MSY, explored r-k pairs with the prior box, viable r-k pairs, B/k with its three priors, F/Fmsy, equilibrium curve |
| `catch`, `rk`, `biomass`, `b_bmsy`, `exploitation`, `equilibrium` | The same panels as single charts, and B/Bmsy (lines at Bmsy, 0.8 Bmsy, 0.5 Bmsy) |
| `management` | The four management panels (Figure 2): catch and MSY, B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy, Kobe plot |
| `kobe` | Kobe plot (Figure 3): path from the first (square) through the intermediate (circle) to the last year (triangle), 50/80/95% regions of the last-year draws, quadrant probabilities |
| `prior_posterior` | Prior and posterior of r, k, MSY and B/k in three years, with PPVR (Figure 4) |
| `retrospective` | B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy without the last 1–3 years, with Mohn’s rho (Mohn 1999; Figure 5; needs `cmsy_run(plots = "retrospective")`) |
| `overview`, `kobe_all` | Last-year B/Bmsy of each stock with limits; Kobe plot of all stocks (sized by catch) |
| `status`, `status_time`, `histogram` | Share of stocks and of catch by status, in the last year and every year; distribution of last-year B/Bmsy |
| `b_bmsy_all`, `trend`, `aggregate` | Small multiples of B/Bmsy; median B/Bmsy and share below 0.8 Bmsy; total catch / total MSY and total biomass / total Bmsy |
| `map` | Median last-year B/Bmsy by FAO fishing area |

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `result` | The result of [`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md) | required |
| `stocks` | Stocks to draw (see [Common arguments](#common-arguments)) | `NULL`: all stocks that ran |
| `charts` | Charts to draw (table above) | all charts |
| `classes` | Status classes: `"fao"` (two classes) or `"palomares"` (five classes) | `"fao"` |
| `annotations`, `lang`, `pptx`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

Status follows FAO (2026) for Tier 3 (data-limited) assessments by
default: maximally sustainably fished (B/Bmsy ≥ 0.8) or overfished.
`classes = "palomares"` uses the five classes of Palomares et
al. (2018), common in CMSY studies: healthy (≥ 1), slightly overfished
(0.8–1), overfished (0.5–0.8), grossly overfished (0.2–0.5), collapsed
(\< 0.2).

## 🔁 MCMC: settings and convergence

``` r

mcmc <- cmsy_mcmc(result)
mcmc$settings        # chains, iterations, burn-in, thinning and draws kept of each stock
mcmc$diagnostics     # posterior summary, Rhat and effective sample size of each parameter
cmsy_mcmc(result, colors = c("grey30", "#D7191C"))   # other colours for the chains
```

CMSY++ samples the posterior with JAGS by Markov chain Monte Carlo
(MCMC).
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)
keeps the draws of each chain of r, k, B/k, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy (MSY is
computed from r and k, as in `CMSY++16.R`), and
[`cmsy_mcmc()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_mcmc.md)
checks them. **Rhat** (Gelman and Rubin 1992) compares the variance
between chains with the variance within them; at most 1.1 the chains are
taken as converged (Gelman et al. 2013). The **effective sample size**
(`n_eff`, computed with coda; Plummer et al. 2006) is the number of
independent draws that the autocorrelated draws are worth; below 400
(Vehtari et al. 2021) the 95% limits are imprecise. Stocks that did not
converge and stocks with too few effective draws are reported apart. The
chart shows the draws of each chain in the order they were kept (trace:
chains that mix well overlap with no trend) and their densities (which
should agree).

The two example stocks, with the settings of `CMSY++16.R` (2 chains of
60,000 iterations, the first 30,000 discarded as burn-in, one draw in 10
kept) and with 4 chains of 300,000 iterations (150,000 burn-in, one draw
in 50 kept; columns `_long`):

``` r

mc <- rbind(cbind(stock = "PRA_27", read.csv(file.path(fig_dir, "green_mcmc.csv"), check.names = FALSE)),
            cbind(stock = "CAP_27", read.csv(file.path(fig_dir, "overfished_mcmc.csv"), check.names = FALSE)))
mc <- mc[mc$parameter != "deviance", ]
rk <- mc[mc$parameter %in% c("r", "k", "msy"), ]
shown <- mc[, c("stock", "label", "median", "rhat", "n_eff", "median_long", "rhat_long", "n_eff_long")]
shown[c("median", "median_long")] <- lapply(shown[c("median", "median_long")], function(x)
  vapply(signif(x, 3), format, character(1), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE))
shown[c("rhat", "rhat_long")] <- lapply(shown[c("rhat", "rhat_long")], sprintf, fmt = "%.3f")
shown[c("n_eff", "n_eff_long")] <- lapply(shown[c("n_eff", "n_eff_long")], function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ","))
show_table(data.frame(shown, row.names = NULL), n = 20, digits = 3)
```

| stock | label | median | rhat | n_eff | median_long | rhat_long | n_eff_long |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| PRA_27 | Intrinsic growth rate r | 0.459 | 1.003 | 183 | 0.468 | 1.001 | 1,471 |
| PRA_27 | Carrying capacity k (t) | 1,070,000 | 1.002 | 164 | 1,050,000 | 1.001 | 1,254 |
| PRA_27 | MSY (t) | 124,000 | 1.000 | 151 | 123,000 | 1.001 | 1,451 |
| PRA_27 | B/k in the first year | 0.424 | 1.003 | 262 | 0.432 | 1.000 | 1,929 |
| PRA_27 | B/k in the last year | 0.697 | 1.008 | 230 | 0.693 | 1.000 | 1,528 |
| PRA_27 | B/Bmsy in the last year | 1.39 | 1.008 | 230 | 1.39 | 1.000 | 1,528 |
| PRA_27 | F/Fmsy in the last year | 0.579 | 1.001 | 492 | 0.588 | 1.000 | 2,811 |
| CAP_27 | Intrinsic growth rate r | 0.386 | 1.055 | 256 | 0.383 | 1.001 | 2,105 |
| CAP_27 | Carrying capacity k (t) | 25,400,000 | 1.094 | 124 | 25,800,000 | 1.001 | 703 |
| CAP_27 | MSY (t) | 2,460,000 | 1.034 | 80 | 2,480,000 | 1.000 | 524 |
| CAP_27 | B/k in the first year | 0.331 | 1.034 | 216 | 0.326 | 1.000 | 867 |
| CAP_27 | B/k in the last year | 0.128 | 1.018 | 142 | 0.13 | 1.007 | 1,437 |
| CAP_27 | B/Bmsy in the last year | 0.255 | 1.018 | 142 | 0.259 | 1.007 | 1,437 |
| CAP_27 | F/Fmsy in the last year | 1.05 | 1.082 | 262 | 1.03 | 1.022 | 1,926 |

With the default settings the chains converged (Rhat at most 1.09), but
the effective sample size of r, k and MSY was only 80 to 256: successive
draws of r and k are strongly correlated. With the longer chains it rose
to 524 to 2105, while the medians hardly changed (last-year B/Bmsy of
northern prawn 1.395 and 1.386, of capelin 0.255 and 0.259), and the
runs took about five times as long (4 chains instead of 2 run side by
side, but each five times longer). For results to report, run CMSY++
with longer and more chains and check them:

``` r

result <- cmsy_run(input, seed = 1, auto_start = TRUE,
                   settings = list(n.chains = 4, n.iter = 300000, n.burnin = 150000, n.thin = 50))
cmsy_mcmc(result)
```

Trace and density of each chain, northern prawn and capelin (default
settings):

![green_mcmc.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![overfished_mcmc.png](data:image/png;base64,)

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `result` | The result of [`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md) or [`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md) | required |
| `stocks` | Stocks to check (see [Common arguments](#common-arguments)) | `NULL`: all stocks that ran |
| `rhat_max` | Largest Rhat taken as converged | `1.1` |
| `n_eff_min` | Smallest effective sample size (all chains together) taken as enough | `400` |
| `plot`, `table` | Save the chart `figures/png/cmsy/<stock>/mcmc.png` and the tables `tables/cmsy/mcmc_settings.csv` and `mcmc_diagnostics.csv` | `TRUE` |
| `colors` | Colours of the chains: `NULL` (Okabe-Ito colours), a palette name (e.g. `"npg"`, `"Set1"`, `"viridis"`) or one colour per chain | `NULL` |
| `lang`, `pptx`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

The same chart is the `"mcmc"` chart of
[`cmsy_plot()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_plot.md)
(colours with `mcmc_colors`). Results of earlier versions of the package
have no draws: run CMSY++ again to check them. Converged chains do not
mean that the priors or the model fit the stock.

## 🔮 Step 7: projections under fishing scenarios

``` r

projection <- cmsy_forecast(result, catch = 100000)
```

`CMSY++16.R` has no projection, so
[`cmsy_forecast()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_forecast.md)
projects with the CMSY++ model itself (Schaefer surplus production with
productivity declining below 0.25 k), from the posterior draws of r, k
and last-year B/k of the same MCMC iterations, with lognormal process
error of standard deviation `sigma` (0.1 by default, the value
`CMSY++16.R` gives to its setting `sigmaR`, which the model itself does
not use: it estimates its process error). As in CMSY++, the biomass of a
year is the biomass before that year’s catch, F is the catch divided by
that biomass, and F/Fmsy uses an Fmsy reduced linearly below half of
Bmsy. The last year of the data keeps its catch; from the first
projected year on, the catch of an F scenario is the scenario F times
the biomass of the same year, so F/Fmsy is the scenario value. The
default scenarios are 0.5, 0.6, 0.8 and 0.95 Fmsy (as in Froese et
al. 2018) and the last-year fishing mortality; constant catches can be
added (`catch`). Stocks whose data end in different years are each
projected from their own last year to the same final year.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `result` | The result of [`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md) | required |
| `stocks` | Stocks to project (see [Common arguments](#common-arguments)) | `NULL`: all stocks that ran |
| `years` | Number of years to project after the latest last year of the stocks | `10` |
| `f` | Fishing mortality scenarios as multiples of Fmsy | `c(0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 0.95)` |
| `status_quo` | Also project the last-year fishing mortality | `TRUE` |
| `catch` | Constant catches to project (tonnes per year) | `NULL` |
| `sigma` | Standard deviation of the lognormal process error | `0.1` |
| `seed` | Random seed | `NULL` |
| `plot` | Save the charts `figures/png/cmsy/<stock>/forecast.png` and `figures/png/cmsy/summary/forecast_share.png` | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save `tables/cmsy/forecast.csv` and `forecast_share.csv` | `TRUE` |
| `lang`, `annotations`, `pptx`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

It returns `projection` (by stock, scenario and year: median B/Bmsy,
F/Fmsy and catch with 95% limits, and the probability that B is at least
Bmsy) and `share` (by scenario and year: share of stocks at or above
Bmsy, with 95% limits, and the number of stocks `n_stocks`; from the
latest last year of the stocks on).

With constant catches near the MSY of each stock (100,000 t for northern
prawn, 2,000,000 t for capelin) and the F scenarios:

![green_forecast.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![overfished_forecast.png](data:image/png;base64,)

## 🔍 Step 8: compare runs or other assessments

``` r

result_1950 <- cmsy_run(input, stocks = "PRA_27", seed = 1)        # starting in 1950
cmsy_compare(`1950` = result_1950, `CMSY++` = result, stocks = "PRA_27")
```

[`cmsy_compare()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_compare.md)
draws several runs (e.g. different start years or priors, a sensitivity
analysis) and other estimates (`external`, e.g. B/Bmsy from ICES, JABBA
or a paper) together and lists their last-year values. The start year
matters. Started in 1950, northern prawn has a last-year B/Bmsy of 0.82,
below Bmsy; started in 1980 as CMSY++ suggests, 1.39, above it. Capelin
is overfished from either start year (0.25 from 1950, 0.26 from 1970):

![green_compare.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![overfished_compare.png](data:image/png;base64,)

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `...` | Results of [`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md), named or not (e.g. `default = run1, start_1980 = run2`) |  |
| `stocks` | Stocks to draw (see [Common arguments](#common-arguments)) | `NULL`: all stocks that ran |
| `external` | Data frame of other estimates, with columns `Stock`, `Year`, `B_Bmsy` (optionally `F_Fmsy`) and `source` (the name shown in the legend) | `NULL` |
| `lang`, `annotations`, `pptx`, `silent` | See [Common arguments](#common-arguments) |  |

The charts are saved as `figures/png/cmsy/compare/<stock>.png`; the
function returns `last_year` (one row per stock and run) and `plots`.

## ⚙️ The settings of CMSY++

CMSY++ has a set of general settings, such as the catch observation
error `CV.C` and the number of MCMC chains and iterations. Two of them,
`sigmaR` and `ni`, are set in `CMSY++16.R` but not used by its code (the
model estimates its process error with the prior
`itau2 ~ dgamma(4, 0.01)`): they are listed as “not used” and cannot be
changed, so that a run is not mistaken for a sensitivity analysis of the
process error.
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md)
keeps the CMSY++ values unless they are changed;
[`cmsy_defaults()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_defaults.md)
lists each one with its CMSY++ default, the value used and what it does:

``` r

show_table(cmsy_defaults()[, c("setting", "cmsy_default", "applies_to", "description")], n = 30)
```

| setting | cmsy_default | applies_to | description |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| CV.C | 0.15 | all | Coefficient of variation of the catch (observation error) |
| CV.cpue | 0.2 | BSM | Minimum realistic coefficient of variation of CPUE |
| sigmaR | 0.1 | not used | Not used by CMSY++16.R: the code sets it (sigR \<- sigmaR) but never uses it; the model estimates its process error with the prior itau2 ~ dgamma(4, 0.01). It cannot be changed |
| cor.log.rk | -0.76 | charts | Correlation of log r and log k, used only in charts |
| rk.cor.beta | 2.52, 3.37 | all | Beta prior of the r-k correlation plus 1 |
| nbk | 3 | BSM | Number of B/k priors used by BSM: 1 (first year), 2 (and intermediate year), 3 (and last year) |
| bt4pr | FALSE | BSM | Use the abundance data to set the B/k priors |
| ct_MSY.lim | 1.21 | all | Ratio of catch to the MSY prior above which the B/k prior is kept constant |
| q.biomass.pr | 0.9, 1.1 | BSM | Prior range of q when the abundance data are biomass |
| n | 5000 | charts | Number of points of the r-k cloud in the analysis chart |
| ni | 3 | not used | Not used by CMSY++16.R: the code sets it but never uses it. It cannot be changed |
| nab | 3 | BSM | Minimum number of years with abundance data to run BSM |
| bw | 3 | all | Bandwidth of ksmooth() for smoothing the catch |
| e.creep.line | TRUE | charts | Show the CPUE not corrected for effort creep in the biomass chart |
| select.yr | NA | output | Year for which B, F, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy are also reported (NA: none) |
| n.chains | 2 | all | Number of MCMC chains (JAGS) |
| n.iter | 60000 | all | Number of MCMC iterations per chain (JAGS) |
| n.burnin | 30000 | all | Number of burn-in iterations (JAGS) |
| n.thin | 10 | all | Thinning of the MCMC chains (JAGS) |

Settings marked “BSM” only matter with abundance data (CPUE or biomass);
with FAO catch data only those marked “all” affect the results. To
change some, give only those in `settings`; the others keep their CMSY++
values, and every value is checked (name, range, enough MCMC draws):

``` r

cmsy_defaults(list(CV.C = 0.2, n.iter = 100000, n.burnin = 50000))[c(1, 17, 18), c("setting", "cmsy_default", "used", "changed")]
#>     setting cmsy_default   used changed
#> 1      CV.C         0.15    0.2    TRUE
#> 17   n.iter        60000 100000    TRUE
#> 18 n.burnin        30000  50000    TRUE
```

``` r

result <- cmsy_run(input, stocks = "PRA_27", seed = 1, auto_start = TRUE,
                   settings = list(CV.C = 0.2, n.iter = 100000, n.burnin = 50000))
result$settings[result$settings$changed, ]          # the changed settings
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `settings` | Named list of changed settings, e.g. `list(CV.C = 0.2)`, shown next to the defaults and checked | [`list()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html) |
| `lang` | Language of the `description` column: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |

The settings used are saved in `settings_used.csv` of the run folder and
recorded in `result$settings` and `result$sources`. The chart and output
switches of CMSY++ (`mgraphs`, `kobe.plot`, `retros`, …) are set by the
`plots` argument of
[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md),
not in `settings`.

## 🖥️ Windows, macOS and Linux

The same code runs on all three systems:
[`cmsy_system()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_system.md)
detects the system and makes the changes it needs (on macOS, no
`windows()` and no `antialias = "cleartype"`; see Step 1), and the JAGS
installer is chosen for the system and R version. Each change to the
CMSY code is checked by the GitHub Actions workflow
“CMSY-cross-platform” on Windows, macOS and Linux: it downloads and
installs the matching JAGS with
[`cmsy_download_jags()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_download_jags.md),
runs CMSY++ for real, runs all CMSY tests and keeps the output of each
system.

Results of the check in October 2026, made on two stocks of area 34, the
example area of this article at the time (all 170 tests pass for each
combination; same seed;
[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
on bigeye grunt GRB_34 and sardine PIL_34):

| System | R | JAGS | rjags | GRB_34 B/Bmsy | GRB_34 F/Fmsy | PIL_34 B/Bmsy | PIL_34 F/Fmsy |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| Windows | 4.6.1 | 4.3.2 | 4-17 | 1.422 | 0.639 | 0.706 | 1.391 |
| Windows | 4.4.3 | 4.3.1 | 4-17 | 1.422 | 0.639 | 0.706 | 1.391 |
| Windows | 4.3.3 | 4.3.1 | 4-17 | 1.422 | 0.639 | 0.706 | 1.391 |
| Windows | 4.2.3 | 4.3.1 | 4-17 | 1.422 | 0.639 | 0.706 | 1.391 |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | 4.6.1 | 4.3.2 | 4-17 | 1.422 | 0.639 | 0.706 | 1.391 |
| Ubuntu | 4.6.1 | 4.3.2 (apt) | 4-17 | 1.422 | 0.639 | 0.706 | 1.391 |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | 4.2.3 | 4.3.1 | 4-15 | 1.366 | 0.663 | 0.745 | 1.306 |
| Windows | 4.6.1 | 5.0.0 | 5-3 | 1.392 | 0.672 | 0.740 | 1.317 |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | 4.6.1 | 5.0.0 | 5-3 | 1.392 | 0.672 | 0.740 | 1.317 |

With the same JAGS 4.3.x and rjags 4-17, the results are identical on
all three systems. JAGS 5 or an older rjags draws different MCMC
samples, so the numbers differ slightly (B/Bmsy of GRB_34 from 1.37 to
1.42, all inside its 95% interval 1.08–1.65), but the status of both
stocks is the same: GRB_34 maximally sustainably fished, PIL_34
overfished. To repeat a result exactly, use the same JAGS and rjags
versions; they are recorded in `result$sources` and
`tables/sources.csv`.

## ⏱️ Progress bars and silent

[`cmsy_run()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_run.md),
[`cmsy_plot()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_plot.md),
[`cmsy_forecast()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_forecast.md)
and
[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
show progress bars such as

    CMSY++ [==================            ] 18/30 ( 60%) 00:51 elapsed, 00:34 left COD_27

All CMSY functions that print have a `silent` argument: with
`silent = TRUE` they print no progress bars or messages
([`cmsy_setup()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_setup.md)
still asks before installing). `fao_settings(silent = TRUE)` sets the
session default.

## 📝 In the Word report

[`fao_report()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_report.md)
assesses the main species of the area with CMSY++ when `cmsy = TRUE`
(see [📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and
PDF](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/report.md)),
and adds a part on the assessment with the results of every species and
appendix tables of the reference points, the priors and their sources.
It runs
[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
on the `top_n` main species of the report (10 by default), without
projections. The settings of
[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
and
[`cmsy_input()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_input.md)
are given with the prefix `cmsy_`, e.g. `cmsy_top = 5`,
`cmsy_default_resilience = "Medium"` or
`cmsy_settings = list(n.iter = 100000)`. All CMSY++ results (runs,
charts and tables) are kept in the folder `cmsy/` next to the report,
with `cmsy_result.rds`, so the report can be written again without
running CMSY++: `cmsy = readRDS("cmsy/<area>/cmsy_result.rds")`, with
the path from the working directory (by default
`reports/cmsy/<area>/cmsy_result.rds`). The result of an earlier
[`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md)
run can be given in the same way.

``` r

report <- fao_report(27, cmsy = TRUE, cmsy_top = 5)
report$cmsy_reference_points                  # r, k, MSY, B/Bmsy, ... with 95% limits
fao_report(27, cmsy = readRDS("reports/cmsy/Atlantic__Northeast/cmsy_result.rds"))
```
